title: Why selling to the mid-market is the worst of both worlds (and what WP Engine learned)
summary: Jason Cohen argues that mid-sized companies combine large-company bureaucracy and slow sales cycles with small-company budgets, so the reward rarely justifies the effort. He also says "mid-sized" isn't a real market segment, and uses his early WP Engine thinking to show why focusing on one end of a market lets you optimize the whole business.

principles.text: Mid-market is the worst of both worlds: big-company sales friction, small-company budgets.
principles.quote: But the reality is **it's the worst of both worlds.**

principles.text: Mid-sized firms resist change; fear of change outweighs the upside of improvement.
principles.quote: Shackled by budgets and internal politics, technology changes require expensive coordination and retraining, and **fear of change trumps potential rewards from improvement.**

principles.text: Sales effort is roughly the same for 75 seats or 750, so small deals mean much more work per revenue dollar.
principles.quote: And since the sales effort isn't much different between selling 75 seats or 750, this is a lot more work for the revenue.

principles.text: Company size isn't a market segment; industry and the problem being solved define who you sell to.
principles.quote: "Mid-sized companies" have less in common than you'd think; it's much more important to know what industry they're in, or what problems they're trying to solve, and in what manner.

principles.text: Don't assume a gap between small and large is an opportunity; incumbents may have skipped it because it isn't cost-effective.
principles.quote: But there isn't *necessarily* an opportunity. Maybe those competitors have figured out that it's not cost-effective to sell to the middle.

principles.text: Pick one end of the market so hiring, automation, marketing and sales can be optimized around it.
principles.quote: If we chose just one or the other, we could optimize the rest of the business around it--hiring, automation, marketing, sales--and maybe we should
